prompt: A stop sign is a regular octagon ($8$ equal sides and angles). What is the measure of each interior angle, in degrees?
hint: Begin with the total of all the interior angles of an octagon. Then think about how a regular shape shares that total.

hints.text: Begin with the total of all the interior angles of an octagon. Then think about how a regular shape shares that total.
The sum is $(8 - 2) \times 180 = 1080^\circ$. The eight angles are equal, so divide that sum by $8$.

explanation: The interior angles of an octagon add to $(8 - 2) \times 180 = 6 \times 180 = 1080^\circ$.
A regular octagon has $8$ equal angles, so each one is the total divided by $8$.
That gives $1080 \div 8 = 135$, so each interior angle of the stop sign is $135^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Through the exterior angle
steps: Interior and exterior angles at a corner form a straight line, so the interior angle is $180 - 45 = 135^\circ$ — same answer, fewer steps.
